time.title: Mills and rail
time.note: The railroads have reached the city; the canal and mills line the river below Main Street.

curated.name: Great Turning Basin, James River & Kanawha Canal
curated.note: The canal's Great Basin covered three blocks between Cary and Canal Streets, from 8th to 12th Street. Completed about 1800, and still drawn on the 1886 Sanborn map; later filled and used as a rail yard after the railroad took over the canal (the end date here is approximate). The James Center stands on the site.

curated.name: Libby Prison (warehouses, 1845–52; prison 1862–65)
curated.note: Three brick warehouses, each 110 × 44 ft and four stories, on the east side of 20th Street between Cary and Dock. Used as a Confederate prison 1862–65; dismantled in 1889 and re-erected in Chicago. Footprint from the published dimensions, placed at the corner; not surveyed.

curated.name: Lumpkin's Jail (slave-trading complex)
curated.note: The largest of Richmond's slave jails, in the slave-trading district of Shockoe Bottom: a two-and-a-half-story brick building about 41 ft long, operated from the 1830s until 1865 and demolished by 1876. Its foundations were excavated in 2008 beside Main Street Station. Footprint approximate; position from the historical marker.

curated.name: Shockoe Creek (open stream)
curated.note: The creek ran open between present-day 15th and 16th Streets, dividing the town, until it was enclosed in a culvert in 1877. Course approximated as midway between the two streets.
